What converts on service and mobility websites, section by section

A study of marketing websites only: how ride-hailing, delivery, home-service and app-first brands build each part of the page, which patterns turn visitors into downloads or bookings, and what ONGO should use.

UberDoorDashFreshaAirtaskerClassPassOpenTableZiplineZooxTravelPerkHimsVanMoofPayPalKlarnaWiseHeadspaceAirbnbLumaMonarchBumble
Summary

Six things that separate the best sites

1. The hero starts the taskUber, DoorDash, OpenTable and Fresha open with the booking input itself. Visitors act before they read.
2. Proof sits next to the buttonFresha shows "217,913 appointments booked today" under its search; Airtasker puts "4.5/5, 9,200+ reviews" in the hero; Klarna's CTA carries "4.9 on App Store".
3. Real product, not stock photosHims, Fresha, PayPal and Zipline show the actual app screens, often in a hand, so visitors know what they will get.
4. Trust is explained, not claimedAirtasker's "Only release payment when the task is completed" and Wise's three plain guarantees answer the fear directly.
5. Desktop gets a QR codeUber, Klarna, Ramp, Luma, Fresha and PayPal put a scannable code in the download block, since a laptop can't install an app.
6. Every section ends in an actionAirtasker's trust block ends in "Post your task for free"; PayPal's feature cards end in "Get the App". No dead-end sections.
1 · Hero

Task-first heroes

The first field is the product: a route, an address, a treatment and time. Whatever the visitor types carries into the next step.

Service-marketplace heroes

Home-service sites pair a human photo with a booking card that floats over it, and put a rating right under the headline.

App-download heroes

When the product only lives in the app, the hero becomes the download: headline, store buttons, the app in a hand.

PatternFrequent-use services lead with the task; app-only products lead with the download. Both keep one primary button and add proof (a rating or a live count) within a glance of it.
For ONGOUse a task hero: "Where's your car?" location field with "See prices", plus the store buttons and a QR on desktop. Add one proof line under it, such as washes done this week or the App Store rating, once you have real numbers.
2 · How it works

Three steps, each with a real screen

PatternThree steps is the norm. The strongest versions crop the real app into each card and end with a button.
For ONGOPin your car → pick Express, Shine, Detailed or Custom → follow your washer and pay after. Use the real ONGO screens on a soft lime ground, and finish with "Get the app".
3 · Product showcase

Feature blocks that show the app working

PatternOne feature per block, one screen per feature, three short ticks, one button. Tracking screens are a favourite because they show the service in motion.
For ONGOTwo blocks: "Follow your washer live" (tracking screen) and "Pay only after the wash" (review-and-pay screen). These are ONGO's strongest selling points.
4 · Trust and safety

Answer the fear in plain words

PatternThree concrete promises beat a generic "safe and secure". The best tie each promise to a moment in the product (payment released after the job).
For ONGOONGO already has Airtasker's exact promise: the card is held and charged after the wash. Pair it with "licence-verified washers (trade licence, CR, Qatar ID)" and "free cancellation", with floating chips like "Wash complete · 45 QAR charged".
5 · Social proof

Numbers and voices, placed where people decide

PatternProof works best near a decision (hero, price, download), not in a separate testimonial page. Numbers get a sentence; quotes get a name.
For ONGOStart with what you can prove now: real app ratings and before/after photos from washers. Add a washes-done counter only when the number is real.
6 · Prices and coverage

Show the price list and where you work

PatternPublic prices with one recommended tier; coverage shown plainly with a next step for people outside it.
For ONGOFour cards (Express 45, Shine 70, Detailed 120, Custom from 45 QAR) with Express tagged "Recommended", as in the app. For coverage, "Anywhere in Doha" with neighbourhood names, which doubles as search text.
7 · Download block

The closing call to action

PatternQR + a short typed URL + a rating, on a brand-colour block. On phones the QR disappears and one store button remains.
For ONGOA dark green band with the lime logo, "Your next wash is one tap away", a QR to [domain]/download and the short URL printed under it.
8 · Questions and footer

Answer the blockers, then hand over the links

Recommended order for the ONGO home page

Hero: location + See prices + QR→Trust strip→How it works→Prices→Live tracking + pay after→Reviews→Doha coverage→Questions→Download band→Footer
